title: Canonical cofinal twisted-pullback reduction comparison data
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and schemes $X,Y$, with the completed coefficient sheaves, constructible categories, strict varying-ring systems, normalized reduction/limit data, completed pullback and signed coefficient lines of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients], [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], [det-sp-normalized-equivalence], [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], [def-sp-tower-shriek-realization], [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels], [def-sf-integral-strict-reduction-model], [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], [def-coef-reduction-limit-shift-data], [def-pur-signed-line-scalar-normalization-data], [def-sf-finite-reduction-computation], [def-pur-adic-source-reduction]. Natural index $n$ means exponent $n+1$. Define $P(K)=f^*K(m)[s]$ using the recorded ordinary K-flat tensor. In section-preserving ell-system coordinates define $r_T$ as the recorded completed reduction followed by the exact realization; its signed line is $r_T(\mathcal O_E(m)[0])$, and the finite source is finite-system inverse image of $r_YK$, tensor that line, shifted by $s$. Define the ordinary reduction counit by exact coefficient restriction, the existing universal counit, and exact realization.

For a ramification datum $\ell=u\pi^e$ with $e>0$, a cofinal model is an exact additive functor from uniformizer systems to ell systems whose sections, restrictions, coefficient actions and morphisms are the actual selected coordinates $e(n+1)-1$, using the identity-induced quotient identifications. A cofinal reduction comparison consists of an isomorphism between the selected ordinary strict reduction and ell reduction, sending each quotient-unit generator to the same generator, and a native counit whose transpose under the recorded reduction/total-limit adjunction is the ordinary quotient augmentation followed by the canonical total-limit unit, together with a derived comparison satisfying the displayed universal-counit square on every flat-term K-flat representative. Its native reduction is the recorded coefficient calculus reduction. A cofinal geometry comparison consists of the identity on selected direct-image sections, with inverse-image comparison its ordinary adjunction mate. A cofinal tensor comparison consists of an isomorphism of the derived tensor functors, an ordinary chain isomorphism sending every selected pure tensor in every total summand to the identical tensor, preservation of K-flatness, and equality of the localized map with that chain isomorphism under the fixed tensor models. Define the native finite source and its comparison by the recorded reduction/shift, reduction/tensor and supplied completed-pullback factors; define the selected finite source comparison by the preceding cofinal tensor and inverse-image factors. Define the realization map to be the actual reconstruction unit followed by total limit of the supplied $q$ and $v$, with the section-preserving equivalence unit inserted.

Finally, Tate reduction data consists of first-power and all signed ordinary quotient comparisons to the recorded finite Tate lines. The first-power map sends $1\otimes x$ to the corresponding discrete-coefficient quotient generator. The signed maps obey the existing zero-unitor, positive balanced tensor and negative dual-evaluation normalization. Include ordinary scalar-model comparisons fixed on every pure tensor, K-flatness of each completed signed line in degree zero, and finite derived line identifications equal to the canonical reduction evaluation, K-flat counit, single-complex comparison and these ordinary signed comparisons. These are definitions of data and explicit composite maps only; no inhabitance is asserted. The total-limit comparison used to fix the native counit is the explicit helper of [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison].
